summary: Backend testing of WBS cascade dependency dates improvements. Created 6 focused pytest cases covering: weekday snapping (Friday->Monday), transitive cascade A->B->C, business-day duration preservation when no estimated_hours, manual cascade endpoint parity, non-cascade when end_date unchanged, and X-Cascade-Updated response header. All 6 tests passed.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/wbs.py:521 - dep_end variable falls back to `from_end_date` when neither new_end nor dep_task.end_date exists; this is unlikely but could cascade incorrect dates downstream. Minor edge case.
routes/wbs.py:475 - datetime.strptime is called inside the loop per dependent; could be precomputed once per _cascade call for micro-optimization.

The auto-cascade only triggers on end_date change; a start_date change alone (without end_date) does not cascade. This matches the spec (predecessor's end_date drives dependent start), but worth documenting.
seed_data_creation: Created ~13 TEST_CASCADE_* tasks under QRIDA project (69ccce9bcb339343050d1d6d) with cleanup fixture that best-effort deletes them via DELETE /api/wbs/tasks/{id}. Some residual TEST_CASCADE_ tasks may remain if cleanup order fails.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_cascade_dependencies.py is reusable; uses QRIDA project id and 2026 future dates to avoid collision with existing production data. All cascade rules verified: (1) Friday end snaps to Monday start, (2) transitive A->B->C works and returns X-Cascade-Updated>=2, (3) manual endpoint POST /api/wbs/tasks/{id}/cascade-dates delegates to same logic and returns updated_count, (4) tasks without estimated_hours preserve business-day duration (3 biz-day dep stayed 3 biz-days after cascade), (5) status-only updates do NOT trigger cascade / no X-Cascade-Updated header set.
rca of the issue: N/A - cascade improvements verified working as designed.
